alt: Natural history of disease from prepathogenesis through subclinical and clinical pathogenesis to recovery, disability, or death, mapped to levels of prevention
caption: Natural history of disease. Prepathogenesis is the phase of susceptibility, before the agent enters the host; primordial and primary prevention apply here. Pathogenesis begins at entry, then subclinical change, clinical disease, and outcome (recovery, disability, or death). Secondary prevention is early diagnosis and treatment. Tertiary prevention is disability limitation and rehabilitation.

topicTitle: Epidemiological Methods, Descriptive Epidemiology, and Disease Fluctuations
alt: Three epidemic curve patterns: point-source, continuous common-source, and propagated person-to-person spread
caption: Time distribution of epidemics. A point-source outbreak rises and falls in a single peak within one incubation period. A continuous common-source outbreak has a drawn-out downslope or extra peaks while exposure continues. A propagated outbreak rises gradually with successive waves about one incubation period apart.

topicTitle: Introduction, Tools of Measurement, and Measurement of Morbidity & Mortality
alt: Steady-state relationship P equals I times D linking prevalence, incidence, and mean duration of disease
caption: In a steady population, point prevalence equals incidence times mean duration (P = I x D). Incidence reflects new cases. Duration reflects how long people remain diseased. Prevalence rises if incidence rises or if people live longer with the disease.

alt: Five-stage demographic cycle from high stationary through early and late expanding to low stationary and declining
caption: Demographic cycle. Stage 1 high stationary: high birth and death rates (India until 1921). Stage 2 early expanding: death rate falls, birth rate stays high. Stage 3 late expanding: birth rate starts falling. Stage 4 low stationary: both rates low. Stage 5 declining: deaths exceed births.
